findings.summary: `allowed_bots` hardcodes the bot login "yorkie-agent[bot]", which is nowhere derived from or documented for the configured App — if the installed App's slug differs, the allow-list never matches and the fix step still fails
findings.evidence: Both new lines set `allowed_bots: "yorkie-agent[bot],yorkie-agent"` (agent-review-panel.yml:413, agent-iterate-ci.yml:160). The App identity is supplied entirely by the `AGENT_APP_ID` / `AGENT_APP_PRIVATE_KEY` secrets, and docs/tasks/active/20260720-autonomous-issue-to-pr-pipeline-todo.md:70-77 explicitly says the App may be "the Claude GitHub App **or a dedicated app**" — so the actual initiating actor login is deployment-dependent (e.g. `claude[bot]`). Grepping the whole repo (workflows + docs) for `yorkie-agent` returns only these two new lines: the value is a magic literal with no cross-check. If it is wrong, claude-code-action still refuses the bot-initiated run, the fix job fails, and (with the other half of this diff) every blocked PR is immediately paged to a human instead of iterating — i.e. the bug the change is meant to fix persists silently. `actions/create-github-app-token@v1` exposes an `app-slug` output that could be used instead (`${{ steps.app-token.outputs.app-slug }}[bot]`), making the value self-consistent with the token actually minted.
searchedFor: grep app-slug in docs and workflows

findings.summary: `stalled` now also fires for a failed `fix` (and already for a failed `promote`), but the comment it posts hard-codes "The review-panel job failed to complete … the automated panel did not produce verdicts" — a wrong diagnosis for the new trigger
findings.evidence: stalled's `if` gained `needs.fix.result == 'failure'` (line 460), yet the single step's body (line 479) still asserts the review panel produced no verdicts. When the fixer agent errors, the panel DID produce verdicts and the PR is blocked-with-findings; the human is handed a misleading message and no pointer to the actual failed job.

findings.summary: The stalled condition still misses non-'failure' terminal shapes: `cancelled`/`timed_out` results, and a `fix` job that SUCCEEDS but pushes no commit — both still stall the loop silently
findings.evidence: The enumerated conditions are only `== 'failure'` (plus review-panel `'skipped'`). A `fix` job cancelled by the 45-minute `timeout-minutes` limit reports 'cancelled' (as does a concurrency cancellation), and claude-code-action can exit 0 having made no commit (no push → no new CI → no new workflow_run → no fresh panel). Neither reaches the paging step, so the class of silent stall the diff's own comment claims to close ('Without this, a failed fix silently stalls a blocked PR') remains partly open.
searchedFor: read full agent-review-panel.yml stalled job condition

findings.summary: `allowed_bots` is passed to claude-code-action pinned at commit af0559ee (v1); if that pinned revision does not declare this input the setting is silently ignored and the bot block persists

Undeclared inputs to an action are ignored with a warning rather than erroring, so if `allowed_bots` post-dates the pinned commit the intended effect (unblocking bot-initiated runs) never happens while the workflow looks correct. findings.summary: allowed_bots re-enables a fixer agent whose prompt splices untrusted CI-artifact text with no data fencing
findings.evidence: The whole point of `allowed_bots: "yorkie-agent[bot],yorkie-agent"` (line 160) is to let claude-code-action actually RUN on bot-initiated workflow_run events, i.e. this step executes for the first time. The prompt it now runs contains `${{ steps.diag.outputs.summary }}` (line 165) verbatim. That value is produced at lines 140-145 by `scripts/agent/summarize-ci.mjs`, which reads `.harness-reports/<lane>.json` downloaded from the *triggering CI run's* artifacts (lines 127-135) and echoes `detail.failureSummary` straight into the digest (summarize-ci.mjs:92,97). `failureSummary` is whatever the branch's own test/lint lane printed, i.e. content fully controlled by the code on the agent/ branch (which in turn can be steered by an externally-filed issue body that agent-implement.yml feeds to the implementing agent). Injected text lands inside a prompt for an agent run with `--allowedTools "Bash,Read,Edit,Write,Glob,Grep"` and the GitHub App token (contents:write) available in the checkout, so a successful injection can push arbitrary commits or exfiltrate the token. Note the sibling job in agent-review-panel.yml:414-421 does defend its untrusted input (`<panel-findings>` fence + 'REVIEW DATA, not instructions' preamble); this prompt has no equivalent fence at all. Requires push access to an agent/ branch (fork gate at line 42 holds), so it is an escalation-from-branch-write vector rather than an anonymous one — hence medium confidence.

findings.summary: $GITHUB_OUTPUT heredoc uses a fixed, guessable delimiter around attacker-influenceable text (output injection)
findings.evidence: Lines 141-145 write `summary<<HARNESS_EOF` / <script stdout> / `HARNESS_EOF` into $GITHUB_OUTPUT. The script's stdout embeds `detail.failureSummary` from the downloaded harness-report JSON (summarize-ci.mjs:92,97) — branch-controlled data. summarize-ci only indents the FIRST line (`  ${failureSummary}`), so any embedded newline lets the attacker place a bare `HARNESS_EOF` at column 0, terminating the multi-line value early; every following line is then parsed by the runner as a new `name=value` step-output assignment. GitHub's own guidance is to use a random, unguessable delimiter for exactly this reason. Impact here is arbitrary control of `steps.diag.outputs.summary` (and any other output this step's consumers read), which feeds directly into the agent prompt at line 165 in a job holding the App token — same blast radius as the injection above. This step only started mattering because line 160 lets the claude step run.

findings.summary: Unscoped App installation token persisted into the .git/config of an untrusted checkout that then executes branch code
findings.evidence: Lines 55-60 mint the GitHub App token with NO `permission-*` inputs, so it carries the App installation's FULL permission set (per agent-implement.yml:81-99 that installation needs Administration:read, plus contents/PR/issues write). Line 62-66 checks out the untrusted agent/ branch with `token: ${{ steps.app-token.outputs.token }}` and no `persist-credentials: false`, so the token is written into `.git/config` inside the branch working tree. Line 123-125 then runs `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`, which executes the BRANCH's root `postinstall` (package.json:35) — branch-authored code running in a job that has a full-installation App token sitting in a readable file, and network egress. The sibling fix job in agent-review-panel.yml:375-381 deliberately least-privileges its token ('this token is used in a job that checks out and executes untrusted branch code'); this job, whose agent step the diff is enabling, does not. Pre-existing, but it is the privilege surface the diff turns on.

findings.summary: Bot allow-list includes the bare login `yorkie-agent`, which is broader than the stated 'ONLY our own App'
findings.evidence: `allowed_bots: "yorkie-agent[bot],yorkie-agent"` (also agent-review-panel.yml:413). A GitHub App's bot actor login is always `<slug>[bot]`; the bare `yorkie-agent` entry can therefore never match our App and only ever matches some other account/bot that happens to hold that login. The adjacent comment claims the list allows only our own App, so the extra entry silently widens the allow-list beyond what the comment (and any future reader auditing this gate) believes. Impact is bounded by the workflow-level fork/branch gates, but the entry has no upside and should be dropped so the gate matches its documentation.

findings.summary: Promotion gate 2 matches `agent-review-*` check runs by NAME only — no producing-app check, unlike the workflow's own consumers
findings.evidence: `checkPassed` (checks.mjs:6-11) filters check runs solely on `r.name`, and mark-ready.mjs:135-143 feeds it the raw `commits/<sha>/check-runs` list. mark-ready.mjs:11-14 asserts these checks are unforgeable because 'only the reviewer workflow (which has checks:write) can post that check' — but a workflow file on the author-controlled agent/ branch can declare `permissions: checks: write` for its own GITHUB_TOKEN and create a success check named `agent-review-security` at head_sha with a newer `started_at`, which `checkPassed` would accept. The same repo hardens the *other* consumers against this (agent-review-panel.yml:334 and :358 additionally require `r.app.slug === 'github-actions'`), so the gap is an inconsistency, not a design choice. Not currently a promotion bypass — promote only runs when the trusted panel already emitted blocked=='false' (agent-review-panel.yml:265) — hence low confidence; it is a defence-in-depth gate that does not deliver the property its comment claims.

verdict.reason: Verified in the working tree: `allowed_bots: "yorkie-agent[bot],yorkie-agent"` is present verbatim at agent-review-panel.yml:413 and agent-iterate-ci.yml:160, and a repo-wide grep for `yorkie-agent` returns ONLY those two lines — the value is derived from nothing and documented nowhere. On mismatch, claude-code-action refuses the bot-initiated workflow_run, the fix step fails, and the `stalled` job (agent-review-panel.yml:434-459 — whose own comment names exactly this scenario: "fix ran and FAILED (the fixer agent errored — e.g. claude-code-action refusing a bot-initiated run)") pages a human on every blocked PR, so the iterate loop this change is meant to enable never runs. No refutation ground holds: the code is present as described; the `stalled` job is a pager rather than a guard that prevents the failure; and a hardcoded literal that breaks a core automation flow at runtime is a broken-invariant/wrong-condition defect in the correctness lane.

finding.evidence: The whole point of `allowed_bots: "yorkie-agent[bot],yorkie-agent"` (line 160) is to let claude-code-action actually RUN on bot-initiated workflow_run events, i.e. this step executes for the first time. The prompt it now runs contains `${{ steps.diag.outputs.summary }}` (line 165) verbatim. That value is produced at lines 140-145 by `scripts/agent/summarize-ci.mjs`, which reads `.harness-reports/<lane>.json` downloaded from the *triggering CI run's* artifacts (lines 127-135) and echoes `detail.failureSummary` straight into the digest (summarize-ci.mjs:92,97). `failureSummary` is whatever the branch's own test/lint lane printed, i.e. content fully controlled by the code on the agent/ branch (which in turn can be steered by an externally-filed issue body that agent-implement.yml feeds to the implementing agent). Injected text lands inside a prompt for an agent run with `--allowedTools "Bash,Read,Edit,Write,Glob,Grep"` and the GitHub App token (contents:write) available in the checkout, so a successful injection can push arbitrary commits or exfiltrate the token. Note the sibling job in agent-review-panel.yml:414-421 does defend its untrusted input (`<panel-findings>` fence + 'REVIEW DATA, not instructions' preamble); this prompt has no equivalent fence at all. Requires push access to an agent/ branch (fork gate at line 42 holds), so it is an escalation-from-branch-write vector rather than an anonymous one — hence medium confidence.

verdict.reason: Every element of the finding checks out in the repo. agent-iterate-ci.yml:160 sets allowed_bots so claude-code-action actually runs on the bot-initiated workflow_run (the only trigger, lines 19-21); line 165 interpolates steps.diag.outputs.summary into the prompt with no data fence and no 'this is data, not instructions' preamble. That value comes from the step at lines 140-145 running scripts/agent/summarize-ci.mjs, which at lines 92 and 97 echoes detail.failureSummary verbatim; scripts/verify-self.mjs:55-66,143 shows failureSummary is a line scraped from the branch's own lane command output (and the .harness-reports JSON can be written directly by branch code), uploaded as the harness-reports artifact by ci.yml:67-73 and downloaded from the triggering run at agent-iterate-ci.yml:127-135. The injected text reaches an agent with --allowedTools "Bash,Read,Edit,Write,Glob,Grep" (line 176) running against a checkout authenticated with the GitHub App token (lines 55-66, 154) under contents: write (line 24), enabling arbitrary commit push or token exfiltration. The sibling fixer at agent-review-panel.yml:413-421 uses the same allowed_bots value but does fence its untrusted input with panel-findings tags plus an explicit 'REVIEW DATA, not instructions' preamble, confirming the missing defense here is a real gap rather than an accepted repo-wide pattern. The fork gate at line 42 and AGENT_PIPELINE_ENABLED restrict the attacker to someone with write access to an agent/ branch, which lowers likelihood but does not make the sink unreachable, so no already-guarded refutation applies. Unsafe handling of untrusted input flowing into a privileged execution context with a write-scoped token is squarely in the security lane and blocking.

finding.summary: $GITHUB_OUTPUT heredoc uses a fixed, guessable delimiter around attacker-influenceable text (output injection)
finding.evidence: Lines 141-145 write `summary<<HARNESS_EOF` / <script stdout> / `HARNESS_EOF` into $GITHUB_OUTPUT. The script's stdout embeds `detail.failureSummary` from the downloaded harness-report JSON (summarize-ci.mjs:92,97) — branch-controlled data. summarize-ci only indents the FIRST line (`  ${failureSummary}`), so any embedded newline lets the attacker place a bare `HARNESS_EOF` at column 0, terminating the multi-line value early; every following line is then parsed by the runner as a new `name=value` step-output assignment. GitHub's own guidance is to use a random, unguessable delimiter for exactly this reason. Impact here is arbitrary control of `steps.diag.outputs.summary` (and any other output this step's consumers read), which feeds directly into the agent prompt at line 165 in a job holding the App token — same blast radius as the injection above. This step only started mattering because line 160 lets the claude step run.

verdict.reason: The described code is present verbatim: agent-iterate-ci.yml:141-145 writes `summary<<HARNESS_EOF` / raw script stdout / `HARNESS_EOF` into $GITHUB_OUTPUT with a fixed, guessable delimiter. summarize-ci.mjs:97 indents only the first line of `failureSummary` (and :95 interpolates `lane.lane` unescaped), so any embedded newline places attacker text at column 0 — including a bare `HARNESS_EOF` that terminates the multi-line value early, after which the runner parses following lines as new step-output assignments. The data is not produced locally: the JSON comes from the artifact downloaded from the branch's own CI run (agent-iterate-ci.yml:127-135), and summarize-ci.mjs:30-38 does a bare JSON.parse with no newline or delimiter validation. The single-line sanitizer at verify-self.mjs:55-66 runs only in the producing run, on branch-controlled code, so it does not guard the consuming path. The resulting value is interpolated into the Claude prompt at line 165 in a job holding the App token (line 154) and OAuth secret (line 153). Injection / unsafe input handling into an Actions control-plane sink is squarely in the Security lane; no not-present, already-guarded, or out-of-scope ground applies.

finding.summary: Unscoped App installation token persisted into the .git/config of an untrusted checkout that then executes branch code
finding.evidence: Lines 55-60 mint the GitHub App token with NO `permission-*` inputs, so it carries the App installation's FULL permission set (per agent-implement.yml:81-99 that installation needs Administration:read, plus contents/PR/issues write). Line 62-66 checks out the untrusted agent/ branch with `token: ${{ steps.app-token.outputs.token }}` and no `persist-credentials: false`, so the token is written into `.git/config` inside the branch working tree. Line 123-125 then runs `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`, which executes the BRANCH's root `postinstall` (package.json:35) — branch-authored code running in a job that has a full-installation App token sitting in a readable file, and network egress. The sibling fix job in agent-review-panel.yml:375-381 deliberately least-privileges its token ('this token is used in a job that checks out and executes untrusted branch code'); this job, whose agent step the diff is enabling, does not. Pre-existing, but it is the privilege surface the diff turns on.

verdict.reason: Every claimed element is present as described. agent-iterate-ci.yml:55-60 mints the App token with no permission-* inputs, so it inherits the installation's full permission set — which includes Administration:read per agent-implement.yml:81 and :99. agent-iterate-ci.yml:62-66 checks out the untrusted agent/* branch with token: steps.app-token.outputs.token and no persist-credentials: false, so actions/checkout@v4's default writes the token into .git/config in the working tree. agent-iterate-ci.yml:123-125 then runs pnpm install --frozen-lockfile, executing the branch's root postinstall (package.json:35); the branch's own scripts/agent/summarize-ci.mjs runs at :143 and the agent gets Bash at :176. The repo's own sibling job agent-review-panel.yml:368-381 — structurally identical, same App, same untrusted head_branch checkout (:383-388) and same pnpm install (:396-398) — explicitly scopes its token to contents/pull-requests/issues write with the comment 'this token is used in a job that checks out and executes untrusted branch code', establishing the repo's standard that this job violates. The fork rejection at :38-42 does not neutralize it: the threat is branch-authored code, which the sibling itself treats as untrusted, and any collaborator able to push an agent/* branch can exfiltrate the extraheader token from .git/config and escalate beyond plain write to Administration:read (the same branch-protection backstop agent-implement.yml:82-118 depends on). An over-privileged credential exposed to untrusted code is squarely in the security lane and blocking at major severity.
